title: 2004 AMC 10A Problem 24
statement: Let \(a_1,\) \(a_2,\) \(\ldots\) be a sequence with the following properties: \(a_1 = 1,\) and \(a_{2n} = n \cdot a_n\) for any positive integer \(n.\) What is the value of \(a_{2^{100}}?\)

solutions.text:
Applying the rule repeatedly, \[ \begin{aligned} a_{2^1} &= 2^0, \\ a_{2^2} &= 2^1, \\ a_{2^3} &= 2^{1+2}, \\ a_{2^4} &= 2^{1+2+3}, \ldots \end{aligned} \] so in general \(a_{2^n} = 2^{1 + 2 + \cdots + (n - 1)} = 2^{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}}.\)

For \(n = 100,\) the exponent is \(\dfrac{100 \cdot 99}{2} = 4950,\) so \(a_{2^{100}} = 2^{4950}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Compute \(a_{2^1},\) \(a_{2^2},\) \(a_{2^3},\) \(a_{2^4}\) and track the exponent of \(2\)
